question_text: Find if the two cubes are alike. Write 'Yes' or 'No'.

reference_figures.label: Cube 1
reference_figures.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 100 100'><path d='M30 30 L70 30 L85 15 L45 15 Z M30 30 L30 70 L70 70 L70 30 M70 70 L85 55 L85 15' fill='none' stroke='black' stroke-width='2'/><text x='45' y='55' font-size='20'>#</text><text x='52' y='26' font-size='15'>@</text><text x='74' y='45' font-size='15'>&</text></svg>

reference_figures.label: Cube 2
reference_figures.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 100 100'><path d='M30 30 L70 30 L85 15 L45 15 Z M30 30 L30 70 L70 70 L70 30 M70 70 L85 55 L85 15' fill='none' stroke='black' stroke-width='2'/><text x='45' y='55' font-size='20'>&</text><text x='52' y='26' font-size='15'>#</text><text x='74' y='45' font-size='15'>@</text></svg>

explanation: In Cube 1, reading clockwise around the shared vertex gives the sequence: # -> @ -> &. In Cube 2, reading clockwise around that same shared top-right-front vertex gives the sequence & -> # -> @. Because the cyclical order is preserved perfectly, Cube 2 is a valid rotation.
